question: Does shared linear spatial structure sufficiently explain false permission574 within the remaining candidate support?
hypothesis: Broad spatial trends, rather than detailed object structure, may dominate the false similarity. Removing their rank2 centered projection may reject574 while retaining true70/1102.
method: Use only archived paired patches at frozen correspondences for all5 cases,3 representations,2 heads and full/detector_and_annotation support. Project centered columns onto the2D span of centered query world coordinates. Keep original channel means in residual and trend-only arms. Orthogonality decomposes centered covariance and variance exactly. Evaluate frozen heads;16 seeded random centered rank2 projections control dimension removal. No selection of channels/mask/degree by outcome. A projected patch is an artificial readout diagnostic, not a valid alternative neural trajectory.
acceptance: All60 full/clipped baseline scores reproduce within1e-9 before interventions; input hashes unchanged.
Independent least-squares decomposition reproduces covariance/variance sums and all main scores within1e-10.

Report false574 and true232/832/70/1102 for both supports and both heads; no threshold/model change. Main diagnostic outcome:574 rejected by both C34 heads in clipped support while70/1102 accepted. Failure retained; controls do not authorize deploying projection.
limits: Spatial trends can encode real object structure, not only background. Preserving means isolates covariance; frozen heads may be outside their training distribution after projection. Outcome cannot prove core weights defective or HOTA improved. Plane structure motivated by spatial receptive fields in Lappalainen etal2024, DOI10.1038/s41586-024-07939-3; exact projection is our diagnostic, not their published identity method.
